review_text_raw:
Midnight Protocol is a desktop/hacking sim, and like all of these games, has nothing to do with actual hacking and is utterly unrealistic.  So this is just a strategy (turn based or realtime, you choose) game where you plug away controlling nodes or whatever.  The game does work but it's needlessly convoluted.  I guess to illustrate this, it takes 1/10th the time to learn how to play an RTS like Command & Conquer for 10x the rewarding gameplay.  And even though it's only a 2D game, C&C also has better graphics than this. 

The game design is somewhat flawed in some ways, with a reliance on procgen and RNG that can make or break each challenge. But mostly the game falls flat hard on a very weak and amateurish technical and visual presentation, and sloppy, and in some ways offensive interface design. 

On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.

The game features lazy minimalist/untextured low-polygon "retro" assets and visuals, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s.  The lack of textures is a method that lazy devs often use to disguise their lack of talent/interest in doing the graphics properly and trying to disguise it under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with.  It's unclear why the developers weren't willing to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets and high resolution textures for the game.  It looks bad as a result of their decisions, and that's just another reason to avoid it.

To make matters worse, there's no mouse input, despite this being sold on PC as if it were a PC game.  This is unacceptable and somewhat insulting.  I know this is on purpose to make it seem like some kind of cool "hacker" game but this is annoying. Don't do this.  No developer should ever dictate to gamers how a game is to be played, ever. 

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

Midnight Protocol didn't appeal much to the people who own a copy of the game, either.  It has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game didn't really capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for finishing the tutorial, trivial to get, but less than 39 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  Hardly a success story, gamers just weren't all that interested in the game.

So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?

Midnight Protocol has the laughable, eye-watering price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Mass Effect Andromeda", "Project Zomboid" or "Stellaris".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

[quote][url=https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/reviews]Developer Response![/url][/quote]The developer has weighed in to inform everyone they didn't read the [url=https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/reviews]Developer Usage Rules[/url] for Steam "partners", or they deliberately ignored the part where Valve says:
[quote]Though it may be tempting, not every review needs to be responded to.  A developer response will frequently draw more attention than the original statement, potentially turning a small issue into a much larger community discussion. It's also not a good idea to use this feature to refute customer opinions. Your direct attention can be seen as validation or a defensive attempt to silence your customers.[/quote]

The developer throws all of their toys out of the pram in anger that someone accurately reviewed their game.  Note that the developer seems particularly upset that I obtained this game before thoroughly researching it and predetermining that I will write a positive review for it.  Bizarre, isn't it?  Perhaps we should only be permitted to buy games if we've already written a positive review for them?  The developer has an apalling attitude here.  No, they won't get a participation trophy from me.  If developers don't want their games to be played and reviewed, they certainly shouldn't be putting them into game bundles, or even selling them on Steam at all. 

And it's not just me, either.  Less than 4 in 10 people who tried playing this game got past the tutorial.  That's a hard fact, the Steam achievments are published for all to see.  But the "developer" doesn't accept reality and instead decides to go swinging at a paying customer who honestly reviewed their game and provided facts about it.  Being angry at the truth is a pathway to a miserable life. 

The developer tries to argue semantics about the gameplay for the game but, and this is really important, despite their breach of Valve guidelines, fails to actually address any of the real defects I raise in my review.  They just wanted to try to argue with a reviewer?  That's a great way to invoke the Streisand Effect. 

It doesn't matter if this game was made by a disabled alcoholic on a TRS-80 in a rusty shed while being beaten repeatedly with a baseball bat, or if it were made by NASA, or if it were made by Rockstar Games in collusion with Bethesda, Bioware and Blizzard and cost the GDP of Tanzania to create... what matters is the product and the value proposition it has for gamers.  If the developer failed to allocate enough resources to the project to create a premier gaming experience, [b]why is this a problem that the customers should have to put up with???[/b] 

Worse, why does the developer demand that people must never mention the quality of a game in the review for it?

The "developer" started feverishly stalking me and reading through my reviews after seeing my honest and factual review for their substandard product.

They then argue that I review a lot of games, therefore this game review isn't valid or truthful.  Huh.  If I changed all my other reviews to positive, would the graphics and gameplay of this crap game suddenly improve? No. The developer seeks any possible angle to throw shade at me personally to discredit my review.  You can see what they are trying to do.  If this was the only review I have ever written, would that change any of the properties of this game or alter the facts contained in my review?  Of course not. [b]My reviews for other games have no bearing on the dismal quality of this failed product[/b].

Nothing in the developers pointless breach of Valve guidelines changes any of the objective facts of my review.  My review stands unaltered.  I cannot recommend this game to anyone.
